whatItIs.text: Mild, creamy common beans — navy, cannellini, great northern — that break down to thicken soups or hold their shape in salads.

historyNote.text: The navy bean got its American name because the US Navy fed it to sailors as a staple from the mid-1800s; Australia began growing it in Queensland during the Second World War to feed American troops, where it was nicknamed 'the Yankee bean'.

howToChoose.text: Canned, look for low-salt versions and rinse; dried, pick glossy unbroken beans without discolouration, which can signal poor drying.

storage.text: Dried beans keep cool, dark, and dry; soaked or cooked beans refrigerate in their liquid. The rulebook has the cooked-bean window and the boil-first rules for raw beans.
storage.note: raw and cooked pulse safety lives in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Soft white beans blend into hummus-adjacent dips, white bean soup, or pasta with garlic and rosemary; mash them with lemon and oil for instant crostini topping.

substitutions.note: essentially a large white bean; silkier
